calas:Ayazma.name: Ayazma
calas:Ayazma.teaser: The south coast's long sand bay under the chapel, the place to swim when the poyraz blows from the north
calas:Ayazma.story: Ayazma is the beach the whole island means in August: a broad curve of fine pale sand on the south coast, shallow turquoise water, umbrellas in rows and a strip of fish-and-meze places behind it. The bay takes its name from the Aya Paraskevi chapel and spring on the slope above it. On a north wind the sea here lies flat while the north coast churns. Come back in late October and the picture changes: loungers stacked away, the kitchens mostly shuttered, a handful of locals walking dogs along the waterline and the sand to yourself.
calas:Ayazma.why: The calmest big swim on the island on a poyraz day; in high summer claim your patch of sand early in the morning.
facts: Island minibus from town in season (regular in June-September); by car or bike out of season, when a winter minibus is not confirmed
Early morning in July-August, before the sand fills; any hour on a north wind
Water, shade and food out of season, when the beach cafés are likely shut
The walk up to the Ayazma chapel and spring above the beach

calas:Sulubahçe.name: Sulubahçe
calas:Sulubahçe.teaser: Ayazma's quieter neighbour on the south coast: the same clear water, no loungers, no café
calas:Sulubahçe.story: Walk on from Ayazma's umbrellas and the south coast goes quiet at Sulubahçe. The sand is good and the water as clear, but nobody rents you a lounger or sells you a beer, so the people here are campers, families with a cool box and the occasional snorkeller working the rock shelves at the eastern end. Like the rest of this shore it is a north-wind beach: when the poyraz blows it lies calm, and when the lodos swings in from the south the swell comes straight onto it.
calas:Sulubahçe.why: The south-coast swim without the lounger rows: come for the rock shelves with a mask.
facts: By car, bike or on foot along the coast from Ayazma
Morning on a north wind, before the heat
Water, food, shade and a snorkel mask: there are no facilities
The rocky shelves at the eastern end for snorkelling

calas:Habbele.name: Habbele
calas:Habbele.teaser: A rounded, shallow bay that stays calm on a poyraz, about 7 km from town
calas:Habbele.story: Habbele is a small, enclosed bay with golden sand, shallow water that warms faster than the open beaches, and a shape that keeps the poyraz swell outside. That makes it the bay families choose in summer: a paid lounger section at one end, a free stretch where you put down your own towel at the other. Look before you step in: sea urchins sit on the rocky patches of the bottom, so water shoes save the afternoon. Out of season the loungers go and it is simply a quiet cove.
calas:Habbele.why: The gentlest water on the island for children and weak swimmers; wear water shoes for the urchins.
facts: About 7 km from town by road; the Ayazma minibus serves it in season
Late morning, once the shallow water has warmed
The free stretch at the far end from the loungers

calas:Akvaryum.name: Akvaryum
calas:Akvaryum.teaser: Named for water clear enough to count the fish: the cove to cross to when the lodos turns
calas:Akvaryum.story: Akvaryum means aquarium, and the name is a description: over pale rock and sand the water is clear enough that you watch fish moving below you without a mask. There is nothing else here: no sunbeds, no showers, no changing cabins. The track down is rough, so most people leave the car at the roadside and walk the last stretch, about fifteen minutes. This is the swim for a south (lodos) wind, when the south-coast beaches take the swell and this side lies flatter.
calas:Akvaryum.why: The island's best snorkelling: come on a lodos day with a mask and fins.
facts: By car to the roadside, then about 15 minutes on foot down a rough track; a summer shuttle in season (seen May 2026)
Midday, when the sun lights the bottom
Mask, water, shade and shoes for the track
Snorkelling along the rocks at the cove's edges

calas:Çayır.name: Çayır
calas:Çayır.teaser: The island's wind beach, where Europe's Formula Kite champions raced in June 2015
calas:Çayır.story: Çayır is the beach for people who want the wind. On a flat point on the island's north side it takes the poyraz head-on, and offshore reefs flatten the water inside them, which is why kite racers rate it. From 23 to 28 June 2015 it hosted the IKA Formula Kite European Championships during the Go Bozcaada festival, with riders from about a dozen countries; Britain's Oliver Bridge and Russia's Elena Kalinina kept their titles. On a windy day the sky over the beach fills with kites and the swimmers move to the south coast.
calas:Çayır.why: Watch, or take a lesson: this is not a calm swim, it is where the boards go.
facts: By car or bike to the north side of the island
Afternoon, when the wind usually builds
The kites working the flat water inside the reefs on a poyraz day

calas:Tuzburnu.name: Tuzburnu
calas:Tuzburnu.teaser: A small rocky cove on the eastern side, with no facilities and clear, cool water
calas:Tuzburnu.story: Tuzburnu, the salt cape, is a swim for people who prefer rock to sand. There is no café, no lounger and no shade, only clear water over stone, colder than the shallow south-coast bays, and a car parked at the end of the road. Older descriptions put it at the western tip under the lighthouse and windmills; that is Polente, a different cape. Tuzburnu lies on the island's eastern side, among the coves that give shelter when the lodos blows from the south.
calas:Tuzburnu.why: A lodos-day alternative to Akvaryum, for a quiet swim off the rocks.
facts: The clear water along the rock ledges

provisioning:The Wednesday market.name: The Wednesday market
provisioning:The Wednesday market.teaser: The week's produce stalls, for island tomatoes, local cheese and jam by the jar
provisioning:The Wednesday market.story: Shop it like a cook: walk the whole market once before you buy, then take tomatoes that smell of the plant, a slab of goat or Ezine cheese, a jar or two of domates reçeli, and in late summer Çavuş grapes by the case. It is a market for islanders, not the souvenir shelves. Bring cash and your own bags.
provisioning:The Wednesday market.why: The one day of the week to buy the island's own produce at source rather than from a shop shelf.
facts: Island tomatoes, goat and Ezine cheese, domates reçeli, Çavuş grapes in season
Wednesday, in the castle square according to the venue record; a 2026 site and whether it runs in November are not confirmed
By the stall, cash only (seen May 2026)

provisioning:Domates reçeli.name: Domates reçeli
provisioning:Domates reçeli.teaser: Tomato jam, the island's sweet preserve, cooked in late summer and sold by the jar all year
provisioning:Domates reçeli.story: Domates reçeli is tomato jam: tomatoes cooked down slowly with sugar until they turn glossy and dark red, sweet, with a faint savoury edge that tells you it was once a vegetable. Turkish food writers trace the recipe to the island's Rum families, and today it is the jar every visitor carries home, next to fig jam, from homes, shops and market stalls. It comes out at breakfast and with cheese. Despite the name on so many labels, it has no geographical indication: the island's registered product is the Çavuş grape, not the jam.
provisioning:Domates reçeli.why: Buy a homemade jar rather than a factory one and taste it with the island's white cheese.
facts: Jam of island tomatoes cooked with sugar; a Rum household recipe; no geographical indication found (Oct 2026)
Cooked when the tomatoes peak in late summer; jars sold year-round
The Wednesday market; shops in town
At breakfast, or with a piece of white cheese

provisioning:Çavuş grapes.name: Çavuş grapes
provisioning:Çavuş grapes.teaser: A big, pale-gold table grape, protected since 2 June 2020 as Bozcaada Çavuş Üzümü
provisioning:Çavuş grapes.story: Bozcaada Çavuşu is first a grape for eating: big berries, thin pale-gold skin and a sweet, juicy bite. In September 2018 the island's agricultural development cooperative applied to TÜRKPATENT, and on 2 June 2020 the name was registered as a designation of origin, No. 497, for grapes grown in the Bozcaada district. A university study afterwards found the gain was smaller than hoped, because the island lives on summer visitors and the variety is delicate. By late October the harvest is over and the vines are bare.
provisioning:Çavuş grapes.why: In late summer, buy a whole box at the market and eat it on the boat the same day.
facts: Bozcaada Çavuş Üzümü, a designation of origin (menşe adı), TÜRKPATENT registration No. 497, applied for 28 Sept 2018, registered 2 June 2020
Late August to September; none fresh in late October

around:Troy.name: Troy
around:Troy.teaser: The UNESCO-listed mound at Tevfikiye, and the museum built beside it in 2018
around:Troy.story: Troy is a low mound of trenches, walls and ramps on the plain near the mouth of the Dardanelles, cut open layer by layer by excavators since the nineteenth century. UNESCO listed it as World Heritage in 1998. The Troy Museum, chosen in a Ministry of Culture architecture competition won by Ömer Selçuk Baz, opened nearby at Tevfikiye on 10 October 2018. Its seven sections show about 2,000 finds from Troy and the Troad around it, the island included, and in 2020 it received a special commendation in the European Museum of the Year awards.
around:Troy.why: Do the museum first, then the mound: the finds make the trenches readable.
facts: Ferry to Geyikli, then by car north towards Çanakkale to Tevfikiye
Half a day for the site and the museum
The Troy Museum's galleries of finds from the Troad

around:Gökçeada.name: Gökçeada
around:Gökçeada.teaser: Imbros: stone Greek villages, olive oil and dibek coffee, by ferry from Kabatepe
around:Gökçeada.story: Gökçeada, Imbros to its Greek families, is Bozcaada's larger partner in history, out beyond the Gallipoli peninsula. Inland from the port at Kuzulimanı the old villages climb the hills: Zeytinliköy (Agios Theodoros), with its stone houses and narrow lanes, and Tepeköy, Kaleköy, Dereköy and Eski Bademli. In Zeytinli the coffee is dibek kahvesi, beans crushed in a stone mortar with a heavy iron pestle, then sieved. Visitors leave with olive oil. There is no ferry from Bozcaada: you go back to the mainland and cross the peninsula to Kabatepe.
around:Gökçeada.why: Take a dibek coffee in Zeytinliköy and buy a can of the island's olive oil.
facts: Ferry Bozcaada–Geyikli, by road to Çanakkale, ferry to Eceabat, then the GESTAŞ ferry Kabatepe–Gökçeada (about 75 minutes). Winter timetable from 5 Oct 2026: from Kabatepe 09:00, 13:00, 17:00, 21:00; from the island 07:00, 11:00, 15:00, 19:00; about 215 TL a passenger (Oct 2026, unofficial listing: check with GESTAŞ)
Two days with a night on the island; too far for a day trip from Bozcaada
Zeytinliköy's stone lanes and dibek coffee

around:Assos.name: Assos
around:Assos.teaser: A temple of Athena on the acropolis above Behramkale, and a small stone harbour below it
around:Assos.story: Assos is the ancient city above the village of Behramkale, down the coast from Geyikli on the Gulf of Edremit. You climb through the village lanes to the acropolis, where the Temple of Athena stands on the summit with the sea opening below on every side. From there the ruins fall away down the slope towards a small harbour at the water's edge, a separate stop at the bottom of a steep road. The site is run by the Ministry of Culture through the Çanakkale Museum, with free entry for children under eight. Come in the cool of the afternoon: the climb is steep and the hill has little shade.
around:Assos.why: Climb to the temple late in the afternoon, then drive down to the harbour for the evening.
facts: Ferry to Geyikli, then by car south down the coast to Behramkale
Most of a day with the harbour
The Temple of Athena on the acropolis; ticket 250 TL on the Ministry page (undated, check in Oct 2026); last entry at the box office 17:00

linger:Çınaraltı.name: Çınaraltı
linger:Çınaraltı.teaser: Tea and Turkish coffee in the shade of a big plane tree, the island's slowest table
linger:Çınaraltı.story: Çınaraltı means under the plane tree, and that is the whole idea: low tables in the shade of a broad old plane, glasses of tea and small cups of Turkish coffee with the foam on top, and the slow traffic of the town going past. The guide's earlier edition dated the café to 1969; we could not confirm that year. Islanders come for a coffee and a conversation; this is a place for the shade and the people, not a desk, and in the cooler months the canopy thins and the crowd goes with it.
linger:Çınaraltı.why: Order a Turkish coffee and sit for an hour: it is how the island takes its coffee.
facts: Under the plane tree in town, near the harbour
Turkish coffee, tea by the glass
No: a drink and the shade, not a laptop

linger:Coffee Shelter.name: Coffee Shelter
linger:Coffee Shelter.teaser: The island's specialty coffee shop and roaster, for a cold brew or a flat white
linger:Coffee Shelter.story: Coffee Shelter is the answer when you want an espresso and not a Turkish coffee. It roasts its own beans, and the menu runs from espresso and flat white to iced americano and a cold brew that Katie Parla singled out on her return to the island. The room is small and central on Çınar Çeşme Sokak, and it is busiest from April to October. Out of season it is worth checking it is open before you walk over.
linger:Coffee Shelter.why: Order the cold brew, and buy a bag of their roast for the boat.
facts: Çınar Çeşme Sokak, in the town centre
Busiest April-October (seen May 2026); winter hours not confirmed
Briefly: it is small and busy in season

linger:Vasil.name: Vasil
linger:Vasil.teaser: Turkish coffee and handmade Aegean bakes, a minute off Atatürk Caddesi
linger:Vasil.story: Vasil Coffee & Bakery is a small coffee and bakery room in the town centre, a minute's walk from Atatürk Caddesi in the old lanes. Turkish coffee comes with something from the counter, and the counter is the point: handmade Aegean bakes, the kind you eat with your fingers and a napkin. Sit with a coffee and a pastry rather than settle in with a laptop. Like most of the town it is at its fullest in summer, and its winter days are not confirmed.
linger:Vasil.why: Pair a Turkish coffee with whatever came out of the oven that morning.
facts: Town centre, about a minute's walk from Atatürk Caddesi
Turkish coffee and a bake from the counter
